---
title: "After the term"
---
By week 12 you hold four case reports, each with a reproduction, an estimand statement and its causal graph, and a specification declared before it ran, and a final project in a repository that another person can clone and re-render. The term chose, for each case, the parts of the [companion curriculum](../../companion/index.qmd) that the case needed, and left out several sections that teach something that none of the four tasks required. Each module stands on its own and says at the top which cases it uses, so take the one that your own work needs and leave the rest. The section "Going further" at the end of each case report also holds exercises that run in its workspace, among them the five analysts placed on the curve, the checks that the curve leaves out, and the replications with new data.

| If you want | Read |
|---|---|
| The other estimators of the course: multilevel models and where their degrees of freedom come from, survey weights in a panel of cells, the same model stated as a posterior, and an outcome bounded between 0 and 1 | [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-multilevel), sections 6 to 9 |
| Results from different estimators and outcome scales put on one axis, the conversion behind the comparisons of Multi100 | [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-onescale), section 10, and [cross-analyst comparisons](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-back) in the case study of the EU-frames case |
| A survey item as the outcome of a model, with clustered data, an interaction and a random intercept | [Binary outcomes](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd#sec-eu-frames), section 8 |
| The causal graph of a panel of country-years, and what no statistic computed from the data can settle | [Causal graphs and adjustment sets](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-eu-frames), sections 7 and 8 |
| The items, dimensions and reliability of the battery behind the outcomes of the EU-frames case | [The items behind the scales](../../companion/measurement.qmd), sections 1 to 9 |
| The claim at the level of respondents, and what individual circumstances can and cannot say about a national context | [The individual level](../../companion/individual-level.qmd) |
| Data with a known recipe, a world with no effect in it, and a design tested before it is run | [Simulation as a method](../../companion/simulation.qmd) |
| Where else data for a question of your own are held, and the access rule of each source | [Social science data sources](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-map), section 2 |
| A record found from the paper alone, as an exercise in reading a public dossier | [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-exercise), section 10 |
| A replication of the EU-frames claim on later Eurobarometer waves | Not taught on this site: the data would be built from the files at GESIS by the route of week 10, and [section 2.1 of the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-repetition) of the EU-frames case reports what the SCORE replication on the waves of 2013 to 2019 found |
| One case taken through a term, with every module that it uses | The [semester track of the EU-frames case](../eu-frames-semester/index.qmd), or its [self-study track](../eu-frames-self-study/index.qmd) for working alone |

The one-day tracks of the [housing-audit case](../housing-one-day/index.qmd), the [immigration-and-trust case](../trust-one-day/index.qmd) and the [cohabitation case](../cohabitation-one-day/index.qmd), and the [short session](../housing-short/index.qmd) of the housing-audit case, are the formats to suggest to a colleague who has a day, or an afternoon, rather than a term.
